title: Forms & Reporting - Transportation
before:
The following are the forms that the Maine Department of Education Student Transportation team requires.

Instructions

  • EFT-00 Transfer Bus to Another District
  • EFT-17 School Bus Purchase Request
  • EFT-18 Superintendent Authorization to Purchase Bus
  • EFT-19 School Bus Cancellation Report
  • EFT-20 School Bus Purchase Report
  • EFT-21 Transportation Safety and Training Annual Data Report
  • EFT-24 Transportation Vehicle Annual Data Report

School Bus Retrofitting Reimbursement

In Maine’s supplemental budget, which Governor Janet Mills signed into law in April 2026, $5.9 million was allocated to improve school bus safety throughout the state. As part of that work, the Maine Department of Education (DOE) is now administering those funds to reimburse school administrative units (SAUs) for the retrofitting of school buses that do not have a front crossing arm. 

SAUs should submit the reimbursement form as a PDF to Staci Warren at Staci.H.Warren@maine.gov. Questions regarding reimbursement may be directed to Cheryl Brackett at Cheryl.Brackett@maine.gov.

 

Transportation Data Reporting

The Maine DOE NEO transportation module collects school transportation reports that public schools are required to report to the state.  It is also a tool that school administrators can use to develop transportation plans and share data with school boards.  The district superintendent, business manager, and transportation director should have access to NEO Transportation.

Districts are encouraged to review the Maine DOE NEO DC&R Reporting Calendar to check report submission dates and the status of transportation reports.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 3 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — Staci.H.Warren@maine.gov → Staci.h.Warren@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 2 email addresses sit in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
